title: Siebie · sobie
note: C1 Block 3, unit 4 (C1-SPINE) - siebie/sobie, the TRUE reflexive pronoun, fenced by name in eight B2 packs and sent here by B2-SPINE O15. THREE NEW STRINGS ONLY: siebie, sobie, soba. THE SPINE'S CONSTRAINT IS THE UNIT'S SHAPE - a2_sie's framing must SURVIVE INTACT, so nothing here says sie means 'self' or corrects anything that pack taught. sie still belongs to the verb; siebie is a SECOND, separate word that happens to translate the same way. The contrast is built as a minimal pair on slide 1 (Ucze sie / Znam siebie) and never as a repair. THE PRONOUN IS SHOWN ONLY IN CASE SLOTS THE COURSE ALREADY OWNS A GOVERNOR FOR - do + Genitive (do siebie), o + Locative (o sobie), z/ze + Instrumental (ze soba), pomagac + Dative (pomagam sobie). That is deliberately the c1_pron_12_prep shape and it keeps the unit to ONE new thing. THE FACT WORTH THE SLIDE is that the form is PERSON-NEUTRAL: one set covers myself, yourself, himself, ourselves, and the subject alone decides which. Half of Kontrola, half of Pisanie and four of the ten Uzycie items are therefore minimal pairs against the ORDINARY pronoun (o sobie vs o nim / o tobie / o mnie, do siebie vs do niej, pomaga sobie vs pomaga mu) - that substitution is the error this unit exists to prevent, and every one of those distractors is a real taught form, never a coined one. NO NOMINATIVE, and it is stated as a fact rather than an omission: the reflexive can never be the subject, because it always points back at one. TWO DELIBERATE OMISSIONS, both logged in the digest because C1 is the last level and an omission here is permanent. (1) THE BENEFACTIVE DATIVE (kupilem sobie kawe, robie sobie kawe) is NOT taught, although it is the commonest everyday use of sobie: it needs the Dative extended to verbs that do not govern it, which is a second new system inside a unit whose brief is a contrast, and AGENTS' load-splitting rule is explicit. Every sobie here sits after pomagac, an owned Dative governor. (2) THE RECIPROCAL READING (Pomagamy sobie = we help EACH OTHER) is named in one line on the closing slide and produced nowhere - the recognition-only treatment, so the learner can read the sentence without a third reading competing for attention. ONE FORM IS SHOWN BUT NOT DRILLED AND THE REASON IS RECORDED: siebie as a direct ACCUSATIVE object has no clean discrimination item at this position, because the obvious distractor Znam sie is itself real Polish with a different sense. Znam siebie appears once on slide 1, once in Dopasuj and once in Uzycie, and never as a quiz choice pitted against Znam sie. ze soba takes the ze-shape c1_pron_12_prep taught with ze mna - same rule, recycled, not re-taught.

intro.title: Two words that both come out as "self" in English — and only one is a pronoun
intro.body:
Nothing you were told about się changes here. się belongs to the verb. uczyć się, nazywać się, czuć się are single words that happen to be written with a gap in them, and się has no case, no stress and no job of its own.

siebie is a different word. It is a real pronoun: it stands where a noun would stand, it takes a case from whatever governs it, and it can follow a preposition — three things się can never do.

English hides the difference because it uses "myself" for both. Polish does not, and the two are not interchangeable in either direction.

rows: się belongs to uczyć — there is no "myself" in it at all
siebie is znać's object — a pronoun in the Accusative
after o, so the Locative — a case, which się cannot take
I'm going to my own place.

intro.title: One set of forms for every person
intro.title_pl: o sobie — o mnie, o tobie, o nim
intro.body:
This is the fact that makes the word cheap to learn and easy to forget to use.

The ordinary pronouns have a form per person: o mnie, o tobie, o nim, o nas. The reflexive has none. sobie is sobie whoever the subject is, and the subject alone tells you who is meant.

So Mówię o sobie is about me, Mówisz o sobie is about you, and Tata mówi o sobie is about Dad — one Polish word, four English ones.

The trap runs the other way too, and it is the more common mistake: Tata mówi o nim does not mean Dad is talking about himself. It means he is talking about somebody else.

rows: The students are talking about themselves.

intro.title: The forms, by case
intro.body:
Three strings cover the whole word, and you already own every trigger in the left-hand column.

Ask the same question you have been asking since the case map: what is standing in front of it? The answer picks the form, exactly as it picks the ending on a noun.

The empty row is not an oversight. The reflexive has no Nominative because it can never be the subject of its own sentence — it exists only to point back at a subject that is already there.

rows: nothing — it is never the subject

intro.title: After a preposition — and the ze you already know
intro.title_pl: do siebie · o sobie · ze sobą
intro.body:
A preposition is where the difference bites hardest, because się is simply not allowed there. There is no such thing as o się or do się in Polish. If a preposition is standing in front of it, the word has to be siebie, sobie or sobą.

ze sobą takes the same ze you met in ze mną, for the same reason and by the same rule — nothing new to learn, just the shape z takes in front of that cluster.

do siebie is worth knowing as a phrase in its own right. It means to my own place, or his, or theirs — the subject decides, as always.

examples.en: I'm going to my own place.
I'm coming back to my own place.
I have the keys with me.

intro.title: Which one, and when
intro.body:
Two questions, in this order, and they settle every case.

Is the word part of the verb — is the dictionary entry uczyć się, nazywać się, czuć się? Then it is się, and it never changes.

Otherwise it is a pronoun standing in a real slot: after a preposition, or as something the verb acts on or gives to. Then it is siebie, sobie or sobą, and the thing in front of it picks which.

One thing to read but not to build: when the subject is plural, the same forms can also mean each other. Pomagamy sobie is usually we help each other rather than we each help ourselves. Context sorts it out; there is no separate word to learn.

rows: the thing the verb acts on
the person the verb does it for
pointing at somebody else, not the subject

quiz.explain: się belongs to uczyć — the verb is uczyć się and the two halves are one word. There is no pronoun in this sentence to put a case on.
A preposition is standing in front, so się is not allowed at all — o się is not Polish. o takes the Locative, and the Locative form is sobie.

quiz.prompt: I'm going to my own place. →
quiz.explain: do has demanded the Genitive since A1 and still does. The Genitive of the reflexive is siebie.
pomagać chooses the Dative — mamie, studentowi, and here sobie. Same slot, same case, reflexive form.

quiz.prompt: I have the keys with me. →
quiz.explain: z meaning together takes the Instrumental, and the Instrumental form is sobą. The ze is the same shape you met in ze mną.
o nim is the trap: it is correct Polish, but it means Dad is talking about somebody else. Pointing back at the subject needs sobie.

quiz.prompt: Mum is going to her own place. →
quiz.explain: do niej would send Mum to some other woman's place. do siebie sends her to her own.
The form does not change for the person — it is sobie here exactly as it was for ja. o tobie would mean somebody else is talking about you.
Still sobie. One form covers every person, and the subject — my — is what tells you who is meant.
pomaga mu means he helps some other man. The Dative reflexive is sobie.

quiz.prompt: I'm coming back to my own place. →
quiz.explain: do mnie is a real phrase — somebody else coming to my place — but the subject here is already me, so it has to point back: do siebie.

quiz.prompt: Dad has the keys with him. →
quiz.explain: z nim would mean the keys are with somebody else. Pointing back at Dad needs sobą.
